The '''2020–21 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team''' represented [[Duke University]] during the [[United States]] [[2020–21 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. They were coached by 41st-year head coach, [[Mike Krzyzewski]]. The Blue Devils played their home games at [[Cameron Indoor Stadium]] in [[Durham, North Carolina]], as a member of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]].

Known for consistent high-level performance under Krzyzewski's tenure, the Blue Devils struggled to match their norm this season. Duke fell out of the AP and Coaches Poll rankings within the first few weeks and struggled to maintain a winning record.<ref>{{cite web |last1=O'Neil |first1=Dana |last2=Marks |first2=Brendan |title=What happened to Duke? Inside the Blue Devils' struggles just to make the NCAA Tournament |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2359480/2021/02/02/duke-blue-devils-ncaa-tournament-coach-k-jalen-johnson-matthew-hurt/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |date=2 Feb 2021}}</ref> The Blue Devils finished the [[2020–21 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2020–21 season]] 13–11, and 9–9 to finish in tenth place in [[2020–21 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]]. Duke spent much of the late season on the bubble, according to [[bracketology|bracketologists]], and ultimately their season ended when a positive [[COVID-19]] test forced them to drop out of the [[2021 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]] ahead of the quarterfinals. Duke missed the [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] for the first time since 1995.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |title=Duke out of ACC tourney; AD says season is over |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/31044751/duke-acc-tournament-positive-covid-test-team |website=ESPN.com |access-date=11 March 2021 |language=en |date=11 March 2021}}</ref>

==Previous season==
The [[2019–20 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Blue Devils]] finished the [[2019–20 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2019–20 season]] 25–6, and 15–5 to finish in a tie for second place in [[2019–20 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]]. The team was scheduled to play [[2019–20 NC State Wolfpack men's basketball team|NC State]] in the quarterfinals of the [[2020 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]] before the tournament was canceled due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref name="ACC Tournament">{{cite web|title=Statement from ACC on men's basketball tournament|url=https://theacc.com/news/2020/3/12/statement-from-acc-on-mens-basketball-tournament.aspx|access-date=12 March 2020|website=theacc.com|publisher=Atlantic Coast Conference}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=McGavic|first=Matthew|title=ACC Cancels Remainder of men's basketball tournament|url=https://www.si.com/college/louisville/basketball/2020-acc-tournament-cancelled|access-date=2020-12-15|website=Sports Illustrated|language=en}}</ref> The 2020 [[2020 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] was also canceled due to the pandemic.<ref>{{Cite web|title=2020 NCAA Tournament canceled due to growing threat of coronavirus pandemic|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/2020-ncaa-tournament-canceled-due-to-growing-threat-of-coronavirus-pandemic/|access-date=2020-12-15|website=CBSSports.com|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-03-12|title=NCAA tournaments canceled over coronavirus|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/28893285/ncaa-tournaments-canceled-coronavirus|access-date=2020-12-15|website=ESPN.com|language=en}}</ref>

==Schedule and results==
Due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|ongoing coronavirus pandemic]], the start of the season was pushed back from the scheduled start of November 10.<ref>{{Cite web|title=NCAA committees pushing for Nov. 25 as the start date for the 2020-21 college basketball season|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/ncaa-committees-pushing-for-nov-25-as-the-start-date-for-the-2020-21-college-basketball-season/|access-date=2020-09-04|website=CBSSports.com|language=en}}</ref> On September 16, 2020, the NCAA announced that November 25 would be the new start date.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-09-16|title=NCAA: Men's, women's hoops can start Nov. 25|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/story/_/id/29900866/sources-ncaa-college-basketball-season-start-nov-25|access-date=2020-09-23|website=ESPN.com|language=en}}</ref> Matchups for [[ACC–Big Ten Challenge]] were released on October 30.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Goldberg|first=Rob|title=2020 ACC/Big Ten Challenge Reportedly Set to Be Held Dec. 8-9 on Campuses|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2910350-2020-accbig-ten-challenge-reportedly-set-to-be-held-dec-8-9-on-campuses|access-date=2020-09-23|website=Bleacher Report|language=en}}</ref> The Champions Classic, which was originally to be held on November 10, was later moved to December 1 and was to be held in [[Orlando, Florida|Orlando]]. However, due to disagreements between ESPN, who was staging the event (and others), over health and safety protocols related to COVID-19, the event was canceled.<ref>{{Cite web|title=College basketball tournaments and events in Orlando 'NBA-like bubble' canceled in COVID-19 protocol spat|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/college-basketball-tournaments-and-events-in-orlando-nba-like-bubble-canceled-in-covid-19-protocol-spat/|access-date=2020-10-30|website=CBSSports.com|language=en}}</ref> It was hoped that the event could be still held elsewhere. It was later reported that the Blue Devils would play their Champions Classic game at Duke, while [[2020–21 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky]] and [[2020–21 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|Kansas]] would play in [[Indianapolis]], due to conflicting COVID-19 protocols by the respective schools.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Crawford|first=Kirkland|title=Michigan State basketball at Duke reportedly to play Dec. 1 in Champions Classic|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/michigan-state/spartans/2020/11/06/michigan-state-basketball-duke-champions-classic-dec-1/6186807002/|access-date=2020-11-06|website=Detroit Free Press|language=en-US}}</ref>

Prior to the start of the season, it was announced that Duke would not play its scheduled season opener against [[2020–21 Gardner–Webb Runnin' Bulldogs men's basketball team|Gardner–Webb]], which had a positive coronavirus test within its team.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-11-23|title=Duke opener against Gardner-Webb postponed|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/30373703/duke-blue-devils-season-opener-gardner-webb-postponed|access-date=2020-11-23|website=ESPN.com|language=en}}</ref> On December 10, 2020, the school announced that it would cancel the remaining non-conference games, meaning games already postponed would not be made up.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Duke cancels remaining nonconference basketball games; Coach K wants team to go home for Christmas|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/duke-cancels-remaining-nonconference-basketball-games-coach-k-wants-team-to-go-home-for-christmas/|access-date=2020-12-15|website=CBSSports.com|language=en}}</ref>

==Rankings==
{{See also|2020–21 NCAA Division I men's basketball rankings}}

On January 18, 2021, Duke fell out of the AP Top 25 ranking for the first time since February 8, 2016. This marked the first time since December 25, 1961 that Duke, Kentucky and North Carolina were all out of the Top 25 ranking.<ref>{{cite web|author=Cassandra Negley|title=Duke, UNC, Kentucky all outside of men's AP Top 25 for first time since 1961|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/ncaa-basketball-duke-unc-kentucky-out-of-mens-ap-top-25-for-first-time-since-1961-201005754.html|date=January 18, 2021|access-date=January 20, 2021}}</ref>
